## Research Notes
Truth map: `research.md`. Decisions carried from the spec: D1 form `<spec>/FR-NNN`; D2 opt-in strictness by
`<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->` (unmarked = legacy, today's behaviour); D3 new specs scoped by default;
D4 own-requirement rows keep the `FR-NNN  STATUS` shape. Two traps found in the code shape the design:

1. `grep -w FR-001` matches inside `alpha/FR-001` (`speckit-helper.sh:482`, `spec-cite-probe.sh:40`).
2. `FR-001/FR-002` (an id list) already appears in scanned files (`tests/smoke.sh:1503,1504,5311`); a
   qualifier that is itself `FR-NNN` is a list, never a spec name.

## Data Model
No data model changes required. Internal only: a citation table, one row per token occurrence:
`file:line<TAB>qualifier<TAB>FR-NNN` (qualifier empty for a bare citation).

## API Contracts
CLI contract of `speckit-helper.sh req-coverage [<spec>|--all]`:
- Unchanged: arguments, exit codes, `--all` skip rule and summary line, own rows `FR-NNN  COVERED|UNCOVERED`,
  `summary:` line wording.
- Added: header line `mode: scoped` | `mode: legacy (bare ids count)`; foreign rows may carry a qualified
  token (`older/FR-007  ELSEWHERE …`); a scoped `UNCOVERED` row may end with `bare: <file:line …> — cite as <spec>/FR-NNN`.
- Citation grammar: `[<spec>/]FR-NNN`, spec = `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*`, matched as a whole word;
  a qualifier matching `FR-[0-9]+` is an id list (both ids bare).

## Implementation Approach
1. **Citation table, one pass.** Replace the per-id `xargs grep -w` loops with a single
   `grep -nHowE '([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/)?FR-[0-9]+'` over the scanned files, normalised by `awk` into the
   table. Leftmost-longest makes `alpha/FR-001` one token, so the bare-match trap (FR-002) disappears
   structurally rather than by filtering. A qualifier that is `FR-NNN` splits into two bare rows.
2. **Mode.** `grep -qxF '<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->' spec.md` → scoped; else legacy.
3. **Own rows.** For each declared id: covering rows = `qualifier == $label` (both modes) plus
   `qualifier == ""` (legacy only). Scoped + no covering row + bare rows exist → append the bare hint (≤3).
4. **Foreign rows.** Every distinct `(qualifier,id)` not counted above, excluding bare rows whose id the
   spec declares:
   - bare: today's logic (`others` → ELSEWHERE, else UNKNOWN);
   - qualified for ANOTHER spec: `.specify/specs/<q>/spec.md` exists and declares the id → ELSEWHERE; else UNKNOWN;
   - qualified for THIS spec (`q == label`) with an id this spec does not declare → UNKNOWN (an own
     qualified citation of a declared id was already counted in step 3).
5. **Verdict unchanged**: `uncovered == 0 && unknown == 0`.
6. **Functions**: `rc_citations <files>` (table), `rc_mode <spec>`, `rc_own_rows`, `rc_foreign_rows`; the
   case arm keeps argument handling and `--all`. Each under 50 lines, bash 3.2-safe (no assoc arrays —
   lookups via `grep -F` / `awk` on the table).
7. **Probe**: same token regex; for a qualified token only `<q>`'s spec is checked; bare tokens keep the
   loop over every spec.
8. **Fixtures never write a literal qualified token into `tests/smoke.sh`**: `tests/smoke.sh` is itself a
   scanned file in this repo, so `alpha/FR-001` in its source is a citation of a spec that does not exist
   → UNKNOWN → this repository's `--all` goes red. Fixtures build tokens as `"$sp"/FR-001` (the
   quote breaks the token). Today the dogfood check would NOT catch a slip: `tests/smoke.sh:1089` matches
   only `^FR-[0-9]+ +UNKNOWN` (a `ghost/FR-001  UNKNOWN` row does not match) and `:1078` discards the
   exit with `|| true`. So the dogfood block changes too: it fails on any `UNKNOWN` row, qualified or
   bare (`^[^ ]*FR-[0-9]+ +UNKNOWN`), with a recorded mutation (a literal qualified token for a
   non-existent spec planted in a scanned fixture file → red).
10. **Spec prose**: every `FR-<digits>` in a `spec.md` is a declaration (`speckit-helper.sh:463`), so
   example ids in specs use a non-digit placeholder; `docs/sdd.md` says so (FR-011).
9. **This spec dogfoods**: its own checks cite `scoped-fr-citations/FR-NNN` (a real spec → valid
   everywhere, ELSEWHERE for the other specs).

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: the citation table
**File:** `hooks/speckit-helper.sh` (new function above the dispatcher; replaces `:482` and `:498–502`)
**Intent:** one grep pass, qualified tokens kept whole, id lists split.

```bash
rc_citations() {   # stdin: file list → stdout: file:line<TAB>qualifier<TAB>FR-NNN
  xargs grep -nHowE '([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/)?FR-[0-9]+' 2>/dev/null |
    awk -F: '{ loc=$1":"$2; tok=$3; for(i=4;i<=NF;i++) tok=tok":"$i
               n=split(tok, p, "/"); q=(n==2)?p[1]:""; id=p[n]
               if (q ~ /^FR-[0-9]+$/) { print loc"\t\t"q; q="" }
               print loc"\t"q"\t"id }'
}
```
**Why this shape:** removes the `-w`/`/` trap at the source (research: `:482`), and the id-list rule
covers `tests/smoke.sh:1503`. File names with `:` are not a concern for the scanned set.

### Sketch 2: own rows by mode
**File:** `hooks/speckit-helper.sh` (replaces `:477–489`)
**Intent:** scoped counts only `<label>/FR-NNN`; legacy also counts bare.

```bash
mode=legacy; grep -qxF '<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->' "$spec" && mode=scoped
hits="$(awk -F'\t' -v id="$id" -v me="$label" -v m="$mode" \
  '$3==id && ($2==me || ($2=="" && m=="legacy")) {print $1}' <<<"$table" | head -5 | tr '\n' ' ')"
if [ -z "$hits" ] && [ "$mode" = scoped ]; then
  bare="$(awk -F'\t' -v id="$id" '$3==id && $2=="" {print $1}' <<<"$table" | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  [ -n "$bare" ] && hint="bare: ${bare}— cite as $label/$id"
fi
```
**Why this shape:** D2/D4 — row shape unchanged; legacy path is byte-for-byte today's semantics.

### Sketch 3: foreign qualified citations
**File:** `hooks/speckit-helper.sh` (extends `:497–511`)
**Intent:** a qualified token naming another spec is ELSEWHERE only if that spec exists and declares it.

```bash
if [ -n "$q" ] && [ "$q" = "$label" ]; then
  grep -qxF -- "$id" <<<"$ids" || status=UNKNOWN          # own qualifier, undeclared id
elif [ -n "$q" ]; then
  qs=".specify/specs/$q/spec.md"
  if [ -f "$qs" ] && grep -qwF -- "$id" "$qs"; then status=ELSEWHERE; else status=UNKNOWN; fi
fi
```
**Why this shape:** FR-007/FR-008; a qualified typo must fail, not vanish (spec US4 negative case), for a
foreign qualifier and for the spec's own. A qualifier cannot contain `/` (grammar), so `$qs` cannot traverse.

### Sketch 4: probe attribution
**File:** `hooks/spec-cite-probe.sh` (`:40`, `:50–58`)
**Intent:** a qualified token names exactly its spec.

```bash
toks="$(grep -ohwE '([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*/)?FR-[0-9]+' "$FILE" | sort -u)"
# per spec dir $name: hit if a bare token's id is declared, or a "$name/"-qualified token's id is declared
```
**Why this shape:** FR-013; reuses the same grammar so the two hooks cannot disagree.

### Sketch 5: smoke collision fixture
**File:** `tests/smoke.sh` (`--all` block near `:1441`)
**Intent:** SC-001 — two scoped shipped specs share `FR-001`; a citation qualified for one leaves the other red.

```bash
a=alpha; b=beta
printf '<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->\n- FR-001\n' > .specify/specs/$a/spec.md   # and $b
printf '# %s\n' "$a"/FR-001 > tests/test_c.sh   # never a literal qualified token in this file
# expect: --all non-zero, "== beta" section shows FR-001 UNCOVERED, alpha COVERED
# mutation: treat every qualifier as bare → beta goes COVERED → red
```

No sketch — trivial: `docs/sdd.md`, `commands/hef.*.md` (prose), `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Constitution Compliance
- [x] **1 — payload never under `.claude/`**: all changes in `hooks/`, `commands/`, `docs/`, `tests/`.
- [x] **2 — every command namespaced**: no new command.
- [x] **3 — every guard mutation-tested**: each new branch (qualified own, scoped bare-ignore, qualified
  ELSEWHERE, both UNKNOWN cases, id-list split, probe) gets a fixture and a recorded mutation.
- [x] **4 — zero-install**: bash + grep + awk only, bash 3.2/BSD-safe.
- [x] **5 — helpers fail loudly**: existing `die` paths unchanged; a qualified citation to a missing spec
  is UNKNOWN (fails), never silently skipped.
- Note (architecture constraint "spec dir name = branch name"): this item was planned on `worktree-HEF-3`;
  the build branch should be `feature/scoped-fr-citations` so `req-coverage` with no argument resolves
  this spec. `req-coverage scoped-fr-citations` works from any branch meanwhile.

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| A literal qualified example in a scanned file (`tests/smoke.sh`, `hooks/speckit-helper.sh`, `hooks/spec-*.sh`) | the repo's own `--all` goes red | build tokens from variables (`"$sp"/FR-001`); comments use `<spec>/FR-NNN` (NNN is not digits); the widened dogfood UNKNOWN match (step 8) fails the suite on the build branch; SC-002 run before/after |
| A digit example id in a `spec.md` | it becomes a declared, never-cited requirement → UNCOVERED | placeholders in prose (step 10); this spec fixed after review |
| `hooks/speckit-helper.sh` file length (778 raw lines, already over the 500-code-line limit) | `quality-before-commit.sh` prints a growth advisory | expected and non-blocking (the file is already over; it does not newly cross); keep the added code small via the `rc_*` functions. Splitting the helper is out of scope |
| Existing `FR-a/FR-b` id lists parsed as qualifiers | false UNKNOWN on this repo | id-list rule (Sketch 1) + a fixture |
| BSD grep `-o -w -n -H` differences | macOS red | `smoke-macos` CI; fallback: drop `-w`, enforce boundaries in awk |
| Adopters' bare-cited specs | CI break on upgrade | legacy default (D2); only specs carrying the marker change behaviour |
| Function length in `speckit-helper.sh` | code-quality delta gate | extract `rc_*` functions (Implementation step 6) |
